items.followUp: Define an ecosystem and a niche.

rubric.description: Defines a habitat as the place or environment where an organism lives.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying it as the place or environment where an organism lives.

rubric.why: Checks the defining feature of a species.
rubric.description: Defines a species as similar organisms that can interbreed and produce fertile offspring.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying interbreeding and the production of fertile offspring.

modelAnswer: A habitat is the place or environment where an organism lives.
A species is a group of similar organisms that can interbreed and produce fertile offspring.

items.followUp: Differentiate between an individual and a population.

rubric.why: Checks that a population consists of members of one species in a defined place.
rubric.description: A population is made up of individuals of the same species living in the same area.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying the same-species and same-area features.

rubric.why: Checks that a community includes multiple populations living together.
rubric.description: A community consists of populations of different species living in the same area.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying multiple populations or different species in the same area.

modelAnswer: A population consists of individuals of the same species living in the same area.
A community consists of populations of different species living in the same area.

items.followUp: What are qualitative observations? Give an example.

rubric.why: Checks that quantitative observations are numerical measurements.
rubric.description: Quantitative observations are expressed numerically and are obtained by measurement or counting.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that these observations are measured or counted and expressed as numbers.

rubric.why: Checks for a suitable numerical example.
rubric.description: Gives a numerical example, such as a plant being 20 cm tall.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a relevant example that includes a number and a measured quantity.

modelAnswer: Quantitative observations are measurements or counts expressed in numbers.
For example, a plant is 20 cm tall.

items.followUp: What is endocytosis? Name its two forms involved in taking in solids and liquids.

rubric.description: Phagocytosis is the engulfing or intake of solid particles by a cell.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying the intake of solid particles.

rubric.description: Pinocytosis is the intake of liquid droplets by a cell.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying the intake of liquids or liquid droplets.

modelAnswer: Phagocytosis is the engulfing of solid particles by a cell.
Pinocytosis is the intake of liquid droplets by a cell.

items.followUp: What happens to an animal cell placed in a hypotonic solution?

rubric.why: Checks the relative solute concentration of a hypertonic solution.
rubric.description: A hypertonic solution has a higher solute concentration than the cell contents.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that the solution outside has a higher solute concentration than the cell.

rubric.why: Checks the relative solute concentration of a hypotonic solution.
rubric.description: A hypotonic solution has a lower solute concentration than the cell contents.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that the solution outside has a lower solute concentration than the cell.

modelAnswer: A hypertonic solution has a higher solute concentration than the cell contents, so water moves out of the cell.
A hypotonic solution has a lower solute concentration than the cell contents, so water moves into the cell.

items.followUp: How does biodiversity help an ecosystem remain stable?

rubric.why: Checks the role of biodiversity in maintaining ecosystem balance.
rubric.description: Biodiversity helps maintain the balance of an ecosystem.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for linking biodiversity with ecosystem balance.

rubric.why: Checks the contribution of biodiversity to ecosystem stability or resilience.
rubric.description: Biodiversity makes ecosystems more stable and better able to withstand environmental changes.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for mentioning stability or the ability to withstand environmental change.

modelAnswer: Biodiversity helps maintain the balance of an ecosystem.
It increases ecosystem stability and helps an ecosystem withstand environmental changes.

items.followUp: Name the main criteria used to classify organisms into the five kingdoms.

rubric.why: Checks two of Whittaker's classification criteria.
rubric.description: Includes cell structure and/or level of body organization as criteria.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming cell structure and body organization, or both criteria collectively.

rubric.why: Checks other criteria in Whittaker's five-kingdom system.
rubric.description: Includes mode of nutrition, reproduction, and evolutionary or phylogenetic relationships.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming at least two of these additional criteria.

modelAnswer: Robert Whittaker based the five-kingdom system on cell structure and body organization.
He also considered mode of nutrition, reproduction, and phylogenetic relationships.

items.followUp: What is nondisjunction, and what can it cause?

rubric.why: Checks understanding of normal disjunction during meiosis.
rubric.description: Disjunction is the normal separation of homologous chromosomes or sister chromatids during meiosis.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for describing the normal separation of chromosomes or chromatids.

rubric.why: Checks the meaning and result of nondisjunction.
rubric.description: Nondisjunction is the failure of chromosomes or chromatids to separate, producing cells with abnormal chromosome numbers.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying failed separation; accept mention of abnormal chromosome number as a consequence.

modelAnswer: Disjunction is the normal separation of homologous chromosomes or sister chromatids during meiosis.
Nondisjunction is the failure of chromosomes or chromatids to separate, which can produce cells with abnormal chromosome numbers.
